turns.reply:
This is a clear case of deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Because you paid Rs 90,000 on 3 March 2026 [[CPA2019:s35]] and the photographer failed to show up on 10 May 2026, you have strong evidence (UPI receipt and WhatsApp chats) to claim a full refund plus compensation for mental agony [[CPA2019:s39]]. 

Your complaint is well within the 2-year limitation period from the date of the cause of action [[CPA2019:s69]], and the amount is within the pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission [[CPA2019:s34]].

I have drafted the consumer complaint for you and saved it as a downloadable document. 

### What you need to check and fill in before filing:
1. **Your details:** Fill in your full name, residential address, phone number, and email.
2. **Opposite Party details:** Fill in the photographer's full name, business name, address in Kochi, and phone number.
3. **Date of filing:** Enter the date on which you submit the complaint.

You can file this complaint online through the government's **e-Jagriti portal** (e-jagriti.gov.in) or physically before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Ernakulam. Make sure to attach copies of your UPI payment receipt and WhatsApp chat screenshots as evidence.

BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, ERNAKULAM / KOCHI

CONSUMER COMPLAINT NO. [PLACEHOLDER FOR COMPLAINT NUMBER] OF 2026

IN THE MATTER OF:

[COMPLAINANT NAME]
[Complainant's Address]
[Complainant's Phone Number]
[Complainant's Email] ... Complainant

VERSUS

[PHOTOGRAPHER'S NAME / BUSINESS NAME]
[Photographer's Address / Location in Kochi]
[Photographer's Phone Number] ... Opposite Party

COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019 [[CPA2019:s35]]

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. FACTS OF THE CASE:
The Complainant engaged the Opposite Party to provide wedding photography and videography services for the Complainant's wedding scheduled on 10 May 2026 in Kochi. 

2. The total agreed consideration for the services was Rs 90,000, which was paid in full by the Complainant to the Opposite Party on 3 March 2026 via UPI payment. The UPI payment receipt and WhatsApp chat records confirming the booking and payment are attached herewith as evidence.

3. CAUSE OF ACTION AND DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE:
On the date of the event, i.e., 10 May 2026, the Opposite Party completely failed to show up at the venue or provide any services, causing immense mental agony, distress, and embarrassment on an important family occasion. 

4. Despite repeated follow-ups and requests over WhatsApp calls and chats, the Opposite Party has failed and refused to refund the amount of Rs 90,000. This constitutes a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

5. JURISDICTION AND LIMITATION:
This Hon'ble District Commission has territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain this complaint under Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s34]], as the transaction and cause of action arose within Kochi.

6. The complaint is being filed within the limitation period of two years from the date when the cause of action arose on 10 May 2026, in accordance with Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 [[CPA2019:s69]].

PRAYER:
In light of the above facts, the Complainant prays that this Hon'ble Commission may be pleased to:
a) Direct the Opposite Party to refund the amount of Rs 90,000 along with appropriate interest;
b) Direct the Opposite Party to pay adequate compensation for mental agony, distress, and harassment caused to the Complainant due to deficiency in service; and
c) Pass any such other order as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit in the interest of justice.

PLACE: Kochi
DATE: [DATE OF FILING]

COMPLAINANT
[COMPLAINANT NAME]
